disputed: Whether Trump's annexation talk reflects a genuine policy goal or is a negotiating tactic tied to trade leverage is disputed; Trump himself has called it both serious and, at other points, downplayed it as commentary. The $200 billion 'subsidy' figure is a characterization of the trade deficit that economists and Canadian officials dispute as an accurate description of a subsidy.

items: In February 2025, Trump confirmed on Fox News he was serious about wanting Canada to become the 51st state, agreeing when asked if it was a 'real thing,' as then-PM Justin Trudeau had warned business leaders. Trudeau suggested Trump's interest was tied partly to Canada's critical minerals. (Forbes (https://www.forbes.com/sites/alisondurkee/2025/02/09/trump-confirms-hes-serious-about-wanting-canada-as-51st-state/))

Trump said he would not use military coercion but could use 'economic force' to bring about annexation, and has repeated the 51st-state suggestion multiple times through 2025 and into 2026, including tying it to Canada supposedly wanting free access to the U.S. 'Golden Dome' missile defense system - a claim Canada did not confirm. (Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%932026_United_States_trade_war_with_Canada); The Hub (https://thehub.ca/2025/10/01/trump-revives-51st-state-talk-annexation-threat-security-deal-explainer/))

Trump has repeated a claim that the U.S. 'subsidizes Canada to the tune of $200 billion a year' as a justification for the annexation talk - a claim tied to the trade deficit that Canadian officials and outlets have disputed as misleading. (CBC (https://www.cbc.ca/lite/story/1.7526196))

New PM Mark Carney told Trump directly it was not 'useful' to keep referring to Canada as the 51st state; Carney has said annexation 'will never happen.' Trump partially eased the rhetoric after their May 2025 meeting but revived it again by October 2025. (Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%932026_United_States_trade_war_with_Canada); Time (https://time.com/article/2026/06/02/trump-annex-canada-51st-state-rhetoric-carney-us-partnership-message/))

Canadian polling (Research Co., June 2026) found 82% of Canadians see U.S. tariffs as a continuing threat and 50% consider the U.S. a military threat to Canada. (BIV/Research Co. (https://www.biv.com/news/commentary/mario-canseco-canadians-reject-trumps-annexation-talk-as-tariff-worries-grow-polling-shows-12392688))

Renegotiation of the USMCA/CUSMA trade agreement among the U.S., Canada, and Mexico has proceeded alongside this rhetoric, with Canada and Mexico separately requesting a 16-year renewal as of mid-2026. (Time (https://time.com/article/2026/06/02/trump-annex-canada-51st-state-rhetoric-carney-us-partnership-message/))
sections.label: Documentation

summary: Since early 2025, Trump has repeatedly floated Canada becoming the U.S.'s '51st state,' alongside a tariff and trade dispute with both Canada and Mexico.
title: Canada and Mexico: '51st state' rhetoric and the trade war
